# Three dependencies resolved by filesystem path, not module resolution — the engine assumes its node_modules is never hoisted

## Current decision and implementation contract — 2026-09-08

All three sites still need delivery at `dev@b537d0a3c8101c7d9fcb2a23317b6133d8d356ec`. PR #17962 was closed **without merging**; its earlier implementation is prior art, not completed ACs. #17997 was closed back into this ticket, not resolved.

**Decision:** keep browser-relative imports and publish a generated `dist/marked.mjs`, following the existing parse5 artifact producer/release/package contract (#17943). Copy marked's already self-contained upstream ESM file and license without recompiling it, include it in initial/release builds and package checks, and carry it from the engine package into consumer ESM output. Consumers must not install the engine's dev dependencies or edit its source to use it.

The webpack binary resolves from the active project's package context, preserving the generated workspace's compiler choice even when the engine postinstall creates its own nested webpack. The original `neoPath` config selection remains unchanged. Parser producers resolve their inputs from their own module context. The webpack runner invokes the resolved JavaScript entry with Node and an argv array, preserving its existing env/thread selection without shell re-splitting.

**Why this shape:** native [import maps do not reach worker graphs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script/type/importmap). A bare marked import would therefore break dev workers. Requiring an unhoisted runtime installation adds a consumer layout constraint without need; the existing engine-owned artifact pattern avoids it. The alternative bundledDependencies layout does not survive the current ESM rewrite: it puts marked inside the engine package, while the emitted node_modules specifier addresses the consumer root. The engine-owned artifact avoids adding another rewrite rule. This is not a new dependency-loading architecture. The published artifact must also survive the existing ESM copy/flattening path; an in-repo success is insufficient.

**Current falsifiers:** invoking the existing parse5 producer from `/private/tmp` exits 1 on `node_modules/parse5/dist/index.js`. A real `npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts` includes both marked-importing source modules but zero marked files; marked is only a devDependency (`^18.0.11`). The source import sweep finds only these two runtime node_modules imports (the Task module hit is a JSDoc example).

## Original report

Three places resolve a dependency by **filesystem path** instead of by module resolution. All three
break for a consumer that installs the engine as a dependency, because npm hoists — and the failures
are unrelated-looking, so they get diagnosed one at a time.

Found while getting dist builds running for a workspace app that consumes the engine via `file:`.
All three still present at `origin/dev @ 8a5fb9c0aa`.

| # | site | specifier |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `buildScripts/webpack/buildThreads.mjs:21` | `let webpack = './node_modules/.bin/webpack';` |
| 2 | `buildScripts/build/parse5.mjs:11` | `entryPoints: ['node_modules/parse5/dist/index.js']` |
| 3 | `src/component/Markdown.mjs:4`, `src/app/content/Component.mjs:2` | `import {marked} from '../../node_modules/marked/lib/marked.esm.js'` |

## These are two different problems and only one of them is a defect

**1 and 2 are Node-side and have no constraint forcing them.** Both are resolved relative to the
**process cwd**, not to the script. A consumer running the engine's build scripts has its own
`node_modules` layout — `webpack` and `parse5` are hoisted to the consumer root, so `./node_modules/…`
from the consumer's cwd may or may not hit them, and the failure is a bare ENOENT that says nothing
about hoisting. Nothing here needs a path: `import.meta.resolve` / `createRequire(import.meta.url)`
resolves both correctly from either layout.

**3 is deliberate and must not be "fixed" by switching to a bare specifier.** The engine loads ES
modules **directly in the browser** in dev mode, and there is no import map anywhere in the repo
(checked). A bare `import {marked} from 'marked'` would simply fail to resolve in the browser. The
relative path is what makes dev mode work — it is load-bearing, not sloppiness.

What it silently assumes is that the engine's own `node_modules` is **not hoisted**. Inside this repo
that holds. For a consumer it does not: the engine lands at `<app>/node_modules/neo.mjs/`, `marked`
hoists to `<app>/node_modules/marked/`, and `../../node_modules/marked/…` resolves to
`<app>/node_modules/neo.mjs/node_modules/marked/` — which is not there.

So #3 is a **design tension needing a decision**, not a line to patch:

- an import map for dev mode, freeing `src/` to use bare specifiers; or
- vendoring the handful of browser-loaded deps under a path the engine owns; or
- declaring the non-hoisted layout a supported requirement and having consumers pin it
  (`nohoist` / an install-time check that fails with a sentence naming the cause).

I have deliberately not picked one — it touches dev-mode loading, packaging, and consumer install, so
it wants a maintainer decision before an implementation.

## Why file it as one ticket

Because the shared root is what makes it expensive: each site fails differently (a missing binary, a
bundler entry point that is not found, a module that will not resolve in the browser), so they read as
three unrelated build problems. Naming the class once is worth more than three leaf fixes discovered
separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `buildScripts/webpack/buildThreads.mjs` resolves the `webpack` binary through module resolution
      rather than a cwd-relative path, and works when invoked from a consumer whose `node_modules` is
      hoisted.
- [ ] `buildScripts/build/parse5.mjs` resolves its entry point the same way.
- [ ] A decision is recorded for the browser-loaded `marked` imports — import map, vendored copy, or a
      supported non-hoisted layout — with the reason, so the next reader does not "fix" a deliberate
      relative path into a broken bare one.
- [ ] Whichever is chosen, a consumer installing the engine as a dependency can run the thread build
      without editing engine files.

## Out of Scope

- The engine's service-thread entry: a workspace build fails that thread for lack of an app-owned
  `ServiceWorker.mjs`, which is expected — the reference workspace has none either.

- 2026-08-31T17:14:02Z @neo-opus-grace cross-referenced by PR #17962
### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-08-31T17:15:51Z

## AC-1 / AC-2 delivered; AC-3 gets evidence, not a unilateral decision

The two Node-side sites are fixed in #17962 (`Resolves #17961`, the narrow leaf). This ticket stays open as the class ticket, because AC-3 is the half you explicitly reserved: *"it touches dev-mode loading, packaging, and consumer install, so it wants a maintainer decision before an implementation."* Agreed — so here is the measurement that decides it, rather than my pick dressed as a finding.

### First, your read of #3 is confirmed at the source

There is **no import map anywhere in the repo** — sweeping every text file outside `node_modules`/`dist` returns exactly one `importmap` hit, and it is prose inside a Discussion document, not a live map. So a bare `import {marked} from 'marked'` would fail to resolve in the browser exactly as you wrote. The relative path is load-bearing. Anyone reaching for the "obvious" fix here breaks dev mode.

### But the fork is differently shaped than "which resolution strategy"

`marked` is declared in **`devDependencies`**, not `dependencies`:

```
dependencies    —
devDependencies ^18.0.5
peerDependencies —
```

And both importers **ship to consumers**. `npm pack --dry-run` over the current tree emits 5329 files, including `src/component/Markdown.mjs` and `src/app/content/Component.mjs`.

So the engine ships source that imports `marked`, while never declaring `marked` as something a consumer install provides. **A consumer does not get `marked` at all** — not hoisted to the root, not nested under `neo.mjs`, not anywhere. The `../../node_modules/marked/…` path is not merely pointing at the wrong place under hoisting; it is pointing at a package that was never installed.

### And there is prior art that removes a second option

Discussion #17247 already settled the import-map half, with a current MDN citation:

> Native import maps still apply to document-loaded modules, **not worker/worklet graphs**.

Both importers are app-worker modules — `src/component/Markdown.mjs` extends `component/Base.mjs`, so its import graph is resolved inside the app worker, not by the document. A `<script type="importmap">` never reaches it.

I should flag that I nearly missed this. My first draft of this comment had "import map: still viable"; it was wrong, and the thing that caught it was grepping the repo for `importmap` and landing on that Discussion — which I authored myself in August. Re-deriving beats nothing; checking beats re-deriving.

### The fork, after both measurements

| option (yours) | status |
|---|---|
| **Import map for dev mode** | **Ruled out** for these importers by #17247's cited MDN behaviour: import maps do not apply to worker graphs, and both files load in the app worker. It would remain the right answer for anything genuinely document-loaded — which these are not. |
| **Vendor the browser-loaded deps under a path the engine owns** | **The only survivor.** It needs no consumer install change and no worker-graph resolution primitive: the file ships inside the package, so there is no hoisting question and no dependency to declare. Cost is a tracked third-party copy to keep current. |
| **Declare the non-hoisted layout supported (`nohoist` / install-time check)** | **Ruled out.** `nohoist` controls *where* an installed package lands; it cannot conjure one that a `devDependencies` entry means was never installed. A consumer pinning a non-hoisted layout still has no `marked`. |

### What I am not doing

I am not recording the decision. The evidence points hard at vendoring — it is the only option left standing — but "vendor it" still has a shape you own: which path the engine claims for vendored browser deps, whether the copy is generated at build time or tracked, and how it stays current with the `devDependencies` version. Those are packaging-shape calls, which is the half you reserved. What I can say is that the option space is now two-thirds smaller, and neither elimination rests on my judgement: one is a `package.json` fact, the other a cited platform behaviour.

Two things worth deciding alongside it, since they fall out of the same measurement:

1. **Whether this is a live consumer bug today.** If any consumer can reach `component.Markdown` in dev mode, it is already broken for them regardless of hoisting, and AC-3's outcome is a fix rather than a hardening. I have not tested a real consumer install — that is #17868 AC-4 territory and outside this checkout, which always has `marked` one level up.
2. **Whether the rule generalizes.** `marked` is the only browser-loaded `node_modules` import in `src/` right now — I swept for the `../../node_modules/` shape and it is these two files only (`src/manager/Task.mjs:9` is a JSDoc example, not an import). Whatever is chosen should be written down as the rule for the *next* one, which is what AC-3's "with the reason" clause is already asking for.

### Also out of scope, but found while here

`buildThreads.mjs` interpolates every argument into a shell string under `shell: true` — `--config ${tPath}...` and the resolved binary path both arrive unquoted, so a checkout path containing a space splits. That is the same class `buildScripts/build/highlightJs.mjs` was explicitly hardened against ("no INTERPOLATED value reaches a shell"), and it is pre-existing and independent of resolution. I deliberately did not bundle it into #17962 — the `--env insideNeo=X worker=Y` arguments *rely* on shell re-splitting today, so fixing it properly means re-deriving that argv contract, and verifying that needs full thread builds. Say the word and I will file it; I did not want to mint a ticket on your ticket without asking.

**Rows 1 and 2 are unblocked and implemented; row 3 is what actually blocks this ticket.**

I briefly split rows 1–2 into #17961 with PR #17962 rather than recording that here. Both are closed — the split produced two tickets and a reviewer request for work this ticket already owned. Correcting it in place instead:

- **Row 1** `buildScripts/webpack/buildThreads.mjs:21` and **row 2** `buildScripts/build/parse5.mjs:11` are mechanical: resolve through `import.meta.resolve` / the package entry rather than a cwd-relative path. A working implementation with specs is on `grace/17961-module-resolution` — cherry-pickable, and not a claim on this ticket.
- **Row 3** `marked` in `src/component/Markdown.mjs` / `src/app/content/Component.mjs` is **not** a line to patch. Dev mode loads ES modules directly in the browser with no import map, so the relative path is load-bearing there. That is a maintainer decision, and it is the only thing here that needs one.

So this ticket is not blocked as a whole — it is blocked on one row, and the other two can land whenever someone takes it. Recording that distinction is what I should have done two days ago instead of routing around it.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-08-31T23:20:03Z

Row 3 measurement, recorded here where it belongs rather than as a new ticket.

Measured on `origin/dev` @ `fa20136f29`: a greenfield workspace consuming the real engine builds `dist/esm` and exits 1 with

```
dist/esm/src/component/Markdown.mjs    → ../../../../node_modules/marked/lib/marked.esm.js
dist/esm/src/app/content/Component.mjs → ../../../../../node_modules/marked/lib/marked.esm.js
```

**Sharper than this ticket's row-3 analysis.** The body reasons about hoisting — that `../../node_modules/marked/…` resolves to `<app>/node_modules/neo.mjs/node_modules/marked/`, "which is not there". The stronger fact is that it is not there under *any* layout: `package.json` has `"dependencies": {}` and carries `marked` in `devDependencies`, and npm does not install an installed package's devDependencies. A consumer never has `marked` on disk at all — no hoisting arrangement, bundler, or `basePath` changes that.

So row 3 is not a path-shape defect that a correct specifier would fix; it is a dependency-classification defect. Whatever destination the deferred maintainer decision picks, `marked` has to become a real dependency (or be vendored the way #17943 vendored `parse5`) for either of these two modules to load in a consuming workspace.

Also worth pinning: `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/esmWorkspaceBuild.spec.mjs` builds against a **stub** engine (`node_modules/neo.mjs/src/core/Base.mjs` = `export default class Base {}`), so no fixture has ever compiled a module importing `marked`. Row 3 is invisible to every existing arm by construction.

No new ticket. This ticket already owns the row.
